workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates

leads.summary: Aliased input roots consume the 500-row budget twice, hiding otherwise eligible media
leads.consequence: A Videos symlink and another root pointing to its target (or a duplicate root) yield two path spellings for each physical file. The cap is applied before deduplication, so later unique files disappear from the picker. On a synthetic 300-file library, the picker received 500 rows but only 250 distinct filenames. The next invocation does the same thing. PR #13197 implements inode deduplication but conflicts at this hunk; -H alone does not solve it.
leads.triage: already in Opus final (C1); corroboration; covered by C1 still_present row

leads.summary: Bounded encoded options can still make the single IPC payload argument exceed the OS limit
leads.consequence: The new guard counts only options_json, while the Perl payload adds an unrestricted prompt plus field names and paths. A 119900-byte valid option and a 12000-byte prompt pass the options guard, then exec of omarchy-shell fails with 'Argument list too long' and exit 126, with no menu and no intended 'options payload too large' error. For command-line or plugin callers that provide a long prompt/list, truncation or checking the final JSON payload before passing it as a single argv element is required; normal fixed short prompts remain safe.
leads.triage: behavioural -> Opus follow-up-1; confirmed (prompt ~11 KB with options at cap -> Argument list too long, exit 126) but identical at base; no in-tree caller prompt over 26 bytes; not published (X1)

leads.summary: Large option lists fail silently when the stock picker is launched from the desktop menu
leads.consequence: The new explicit error is sent only to stderr. Transcode and the RetroArch launcher are invoked detached by the menu, not in a terminal, and no notification is emitted for this rejection; RetroArch also maps the rejected picker to exit 0 with '|| exit 0'. Users see no picker and no explanation and retries produce the same result. Terminal invocations do show stderr. This issue predates the final -H commit, but the newly added size guard still causes it.
leads.triage: already in Opus final (N1); corroboration; N1 still_present

leads.summary: Three divergent open PRs change the same file-picker pipeline hunk
leads.consequence: #13197 adds -H plus inode deduplication, #13018 adds -H plus a 500-row head cap, and #7320 replaces the pipeline with an empty-result check and direct selector input. Applying any of these against this head leaves a conflict in the pipeline. Resolving by taking #13197 or #13018's pipeline without the current byte guard loses the new path-byte protection; taking #7320's pipeline alone loses -H and the protection. A manual combination needs to preserve -H, 500/80000 limits, and whichever additional behavior is intended. Each other PR is MERGEABLE against its own base, but its head is diverged from this head, not stacked.
leads.triage: already in Opus final (C1); factual; corroboration; coordinator confirmed PR states via gh; #7320 head moved to 330d6ef5, still conflicts (Opus)

leads.summary: New symlink test also passes the earlier -L behavior it should guard against
leads.consequence: Replacing -H with -L in a private copy of the command still prints $link/clip.webm, so the only new assertion passes. But -L also descends interior symlinks and can include files outside the designated roots; a test fixture with an interior link to an outside directory gives one extra file for the mutant and none for head. Add a negative assertion for an interior symlink, ideally also a loop, so the intended -H boundary cannot regress without failing tests. The test's own stub comment still says find -L.
leads.triage: already in Opus final (new test item); published as T2 optional test improvement

## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

Follow-up to the [previous review](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12669#issuecomment-5857137709) and the [author reply](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12669#issuecomment-5857165191), checked at `c623a07a`.

**Verified:** `find -H` still fixes the symlinked starting point from #12665 and no longer follows symlinks inside the roots. The tightened test now catches a return to character counting. No regressions were found in the changed or shared code.

| Earlier finding | Status at `c623a07a` |
|---|---|
| `find -L` also follows symlinks inside the roots | **Resolved** |
| Byte-budget test also passes with character counting (optional test note) | **Resolved** |
| PR description | **Resolved**: it now describes `find -H`, the 120,000-byte cap in `omarchy-menu-select` and the new test |
| Error goes to stderr only (note) | **Still present**: code paths unchanged |
| Lists between 120,001 and about 130,900 JSON bytes now rejected (note) | **Still present**: code unchanged |
| Overlapping roots list each file twice (related PRs note) | **Still present**; the reply leaves #13197's device/inode dedupe to a follow-up if needed. #13197, #13018 and #7320 still conflict at the same lines |
| Earlier resolved items (byte counting in awk and `omarchy-menu-select`, escaped and invalid UTF-8, 500-file cap, "500 **or fewer**", symlink test path) | Unchanged; both PR tests pass |

**Verified:** isolated runs with synthetic folders, comparing this head with `073d4985` and base:

```text
layout                                          base       073d4985 (-L)            c623a07a (-H)
real root with nested links                     own file   also follows the links   own file
  (outside folder, file, broken link, up -> ..)            and the loop
root that is a symlink (#12665)                 nothing    listed                   listed
root that is a symlink, with a nested dir link  nothing    both files               own file
```

Relative, chained and trailing-slash starting points are listed at this head. Broken starting-point links are still rejected with `Path not found` before `find` runs. For files under a linked root, the `%T@` and `%p` fields are the same under `-H` and `-L`, and `%p` keeps the link spelling. With synthetic linked `Pictures`, `Videos` and `Games/roms`, `omarchy-transcode` and `omarchy-games-retro-install` receive the files at this head and an empty list at base. One trade-off: a linked subfolder inside a root (for example `roms/linked -> elsewhere`) has its files listed under `-L` but not under `-H`, the same as base. The new comment at `omarchy-menu-file:47-50` describes this accurately.

The tightened `menu-select-options-byte-budget-test.sh` fails at `cbb7a789` (exit 126, `Argument list too long`) and passes at this head. It also fails when only the byte-count line is reverted to `${#options_json}`. Both PR tests pass at this head and merged onto current `quattro`. The full `test/shell` run on that merge fails in the same 14 unrelated files as `quattro` alone in this sandbox.

**Optional test improvement:** `menu-file-symlink-test.sh` passes when `find -H` is changed back to `find -L`, so it does not guard the new choice. A nested link inside the linked root that leads to a matching file, asserted absent from the output, would fail under `-L` and pass under `-H`. The stub comment on line 20 still says "assert find -L worked".

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** Follow-up at `c623a07a`, compared with `073d4985`, `cbb7a789` and base, and merged onto current `quattro`. Isolated command-only runs used the real `omarchy-menu-file` and `omarchy-menu-select`, synthetic folders and file names, GNU findutils 4.11.0 and bash 5.3, with `omarchy-menu-select` or the shell IPC hop stubbed. Menu rendering, the real IPC transport, network mounts and the locale of real menu launches were not tested.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, Opus 5.5 Xhigh technical review and final fact check, GPT 6 Sol Xhigh search for related issues, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.

**Opt out:** To stop receiving these reviews, reply to this comment saying so.
